The present application for grant of compensation, U/S 166 and 140 (
Old) of M.V Act 1988, was filed qua the accident dated 03.08.2016 within the jurisdiction of P.S Chhawla Delhi.
2. Coming to the facts of the case, it is stated that on 03.08.2016, at about 01.00 P.M, Nitesh Mann S/O Sh Mukesh was going on the his cycle on the esteem side of the road.
When he reached at main Chhawla road, near DBO Office, Majar Peer Baba, New Delhi within the jurisdiction of P.S Chhawla, N Delhi.
A car bearing No. DL9CN3957 being driven by respondent No.1 in rash and negligent manner came and hit the deceased from behind.
As a result of which deceased came under the car and received grievous injuries.
Consequently died in R.T.R.M Hospital, Jaffarpur New Delhi.
3. It is contended in the petition that the alleged accident took place due to rash and negligent driving by Anupam Aggarwal.

She was also the owner of offending vehicle bearing No. DL9CN Seema And Anr vs Anupama Agarwal on 16 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199915193/
4 3957, hence petitioners impleaded her as R.1.

4. The respondent no.1 ( driver cum owner ) has filed a written statement stating therein that no accident had taken place from her vehicle and a false case has been registered against her.
5. The respondent no. 2, insurance company has filed a Legal offer for a sum of Rs.3.75 lacs to the petitioners but the same was not accepted by them.
6.

After completion of the proceedings, following issues were framed on 26.05.2016:
(i) Whether Nitesh Maan sustained fatal injuries in a motor vehicle accident dated 03.08.2016 caused due to rash and negligent driving of vehicle No. DL9CN3957 being driven and owned by Respondent No.1, and insured by respondent No.2/New India Insurance Co Ltd ?
OPP (ii) Whether petitioners in the above mentioned case are entitled to claim compensation, if so, what amount and from whom?

OPP. 
(iii) Relief.
7.
In order to prove their claim, petitioners examined petitioner no. 1 as PW1 and an eye witness Sh Rahul as PW.2.
None of the respondents have led any evidence in support of their case.
8. I have heard ld. counsel appearing on behalf of petitioners as well as R.1 and R.2 and also perused the record.

My issuewise findings are as MACT No.2096/16 Seema & Ors. Vs. Anupam Agarwal &

sentences.text: Page No. 7 of 13 under: ISSUE No. 1: Whether Nitesh Maan sustained fatal injuries in a motor vehicle accident dated 03.08.2016 caused due to rash and negligent driving of vehicle No.
DL9CN3957 being driven and owned by Respondent No.1, and insured by respondent No.2/New India Insurance Co Ltd ? OPP 9.
The onus to prove this issue was upon the petitioners.
To prove this issue, petitioners have examined PW2 Rahul( eye witness)
He has deposed that on 03.08.2016, at about 1.00 P.M, he was present at Main Road, Chhawla near Peer Baba Ka Mazar when a car bearing No. DL9CN3957 came from Chhawla side at very high speed.
The car was being driven by respondent No.1 in rash and negligent manner and hit a boy from behind, who was going on his cycle.
As a result of which said boy fell down on the road and came under the car and received fatal injuries.
PW 2 has been crossexamined by respondent No.2 insurance company.
But the testimony of PW2 with respect to accident and rash & negligent driving of the offending vehicle by respondent no.1, could not be impeached.
Moreover, the proof of negligence, while disposing of a claim under MACT, is not that strict as it is under Section 279/338/304A of IPC.

Therefore, the evidence which has come on the file only can be considered.
It is a matter of record that there is no evidence at all to show there was any fault on the part of deceased while cycling.
10. The fact that Nitesh Maan died in that accident is also supported by his MACT No.2096/16 Seema & Ors. Vs. Anupam Agarwal & Ors.

Moreover,after investigation, police indicted respondent no.1 as accused for offences punishable under Sections 279/304A of IPC.
The FIR has been registered against respondent no.1 and he has not filed any complaint against the police before any higher authority against his such implication.

Considering all the evidence as discussed above, it stands proved that accident in question was caused due to rash or negligent driving of car bearing No.DL9CN3957 by respondent no.1 thereby causing death of Nitesh Maan.
So prima facie a fact has been brought on record that driver of the offending vehicle was driving the offending vehicle rashly and negligent.

11. This issue is therefore decided in favour of the petitioners and against respondents by holding that victim Nitesh Maan died in a motor vehicle accident due to rash and negligent driving of car bearing no DL9CN3957 by respondent no.1.
ISSUE No.2: Whether the petitioners are entitled to compensation, if so, what amount and from whom?

OPP.
12.
It is not disputed during arguments that petitioners are the mother and father of victim.
Moreover, this fact is also established by statement of Smt Seema (PW1) mother of deceased.
And being LRs of deceased, petitioners are well within their rights to claim compensation from respondents.
13. Now coming to the extent of compensation.
It is deposed by PW1 in her evidence affidavit that at the time of accident, deceased was 11 years of age.
To assess the notional income of the minor this Tribunal is guided by MACT No.2096/16 Seema & Ors.
Vs. Anupam Agarwal & Ors.

sentences.text: The Hon'ble Supreme Court held that " In cases of child death, the notional income of Rs.15,000/ as specified in the IInd Schedule of M.V Act has been enchanted on account of devaluation of money and value of rupee coming down from the date on which the IInd Schedule of M.V Act was introduced and the said notional income was treated as Rs.30,000/"
The above observation was made by Hon'ble Supreme Court while relying upon the law laid down by it previously in case of Kishan Gopal and another vs Lala and others (2014) 1 SCC 244.

The deceased was a student of VIth class as the time of accident.
Hence this Tribunal is accepting the notional income of deceased as Rs.30,000/ including future prospects.
The accident in question was occurred on 03.08.2016.
